page.layout: One printed page. A diagram (astronomical figure with circles and letters A, B, C, T, S, d, e) fills the upper part. Below it, one text column of running text. Running head at the top, page number at the top right.

main_text.l: Sit T Terra, S Sol, respectu motus medii, in principio Arietis B, ibidemque medius motus Veneris, a. b. c. d. orbita Veneris circa Solem : sit constitutum corpus Planetae in E, videbitur e Terra in A. Exacto anno medius quidem Solis & Veneris motus rursus erit in B, sed corpus Veneris, peragratis gradibus 225. situm erit in d, & ex Terra videbitur in C. Cum autem annis octo epicyclum suum quinquies percurrat, necessario, Solis motu medio rursus constituto in B, & circulo a. b. c. d. quintum absoluto in e, Venus in

page.notes: The figure is a diagram of the circles of Sun, Earth and Venus: a large outer circle with points A, B, C at its top and the letters T (Terra), S (Sol), d and e marked on the inner orbits, with dotted sight lines from T to A, C and d. The planetary symbols (Venus, Sun, Earth, Mercury-like glyphs) are drawn on the inner circles; they are not printed text. The number "225" is set in old-style figures and may be read as 225. The signature "N" stands at the foot, centred under the last line. The final word "in" ends the page and is continued on the next page.
